entries.title: How did basketball begin?
entries.answer: James Naismith invented basketball in Springfield, Massachusetts, in 1891. He was looking for a game people could play indoors in winter. The first players tried to toss a ball into peach baskets mounted above the floor. At first, the ball had to be taken back out of a basket after a score. The game changed over time. Players in modern basketball can bounce the ball to move with it, and the ball drops straight through an open net when a shot goes in.
facts: In a standard game, each side has five players on the court at once.

entries.title: How did the modern Olympic Games begin?
entries.answer: The first modern Olympic Games opened in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Organizers drew inspiration from games held long before at Olympia. The modern event brought athletes from different countries together to compete. It has changed a great deal since then. There are now summer and winter editions, along with sports that were not in the first modern program. The city that welcomes the athletes can change from one edition to another, so the games are often held far from Greece.
facts: The International Olympic Committee was founded in 1894.
The first modern Winter Olympic Games were held in Chamonix, France, in 1924.

entries.title: How do you score in soccer?
entries.answer: In soccer, two teams try to get the ball into the other team’s goal. A goal counts when the whole ball goes over the goal line between the posts and under the crossbar, as long as the scoring team has not broken a rule. Players usually move the ball with their feet, but may also play it with other parts of their body, such as their head. The goalkeeper can use their hands in their own penalty area, subject to rules other players do not have.
facts: Many countries call the game football.
A full team in the usual outdoor game has eleven players, including the goalkeeper.

entries.title: How does a relay team pass a baton at speed?
entries.answer: In a track relay, each runner races part of the distance and hands a short baton to the next member of the team. The next runner may start moving before the baton arrives so both runners are going quickly during the handoff. The baton has to change hands within a marked stretch of track. Teams practice where to stand, when to start, and how to hold out a hand.
facts: Four runners each cover a leg of the 4 × 100 meter relay.

entries.title: How does a team score runs in cricket?
entries.answer: Cricket has two ends of a long strip called the pitch. A batter stands near each end. A bowler from the other team sends the ball toward one batter. If the batters run to the other ends and reach their safe ground, they can score a run. They can run back again if there is time. A ball that reaches the edge of the field can also earn runs without all that running.
facts: At each end of the pitch is a set of three upright sticks called stumps. Together with the small pieces on top they form a wicket.

entries.title: How does a tennis rally work?
entries.answer: A tennis point starts with a serve. The player hits the ball toward the correct service box across the net. After a good serve, the two sides can hit the ball back and forth. A player can let it bounce once before returning it, or hit it in the air after the return of serve. The rally ends when one side fails to send a legal ball back.
facts: Hitting the ball in the air before it bounces is a volley.

entries.title: How does table tennis use the table in a rally?
entries.answer: A table tennis point starts when a player tosses a ball and strikes it so it bounces on their half of the table and then the other player’s half. After the serve, returns go directly toward the far side. Rubbing the ball with the bat as it is hit can give the ball spin. That spin can affect how the ball moves and how it bounces on the table.
facts: A standard game is played to eleven points, and a player must win by at least two.

entries.title: What are volleyball players trying to do?
entries.answer: Volleyball teams send a ball over a net and try to land it in the other team’s court. They can also score when the other team makes a mistake, such as hitting the ball out. In indoor volleyball, a team usually has as many as three touches to return the ball. Players often use one touch to receive it, a second to set it up in the air, and a third to strike it over the net. Players try to keep the ball moving without catching it.

sections.heading: An indoor beginning
sections.text: William G. Morgan invented volleyball in Holyoke, Massachusetts, in 1895. He first called it Mintonette.

facts: In standard indoor volleyball, six players on each team are on the court at a time.
A touch while blocking at the net does not count as one of the team’s three hits in indoor volleyball.

entries.title: What happened at the ancient Olympic Games?
entries.answer: The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia in Greece as part of a festival honoring the god Zeus. Athletes competed in events such as running, wrestling, and chariot racing. The games took place every four years. The athletes who could enter were limited by rules that would seem unfair today. For example, the regular events were for male competitors, though a woman who owned the horses and chariot that won a race could receive the prize. You can still see places at Olympia where people gathered and competed.

sections.heading: Finding the field
sections.text: Modern visitors can see the remains of the stadium at Olympia. Nearby are ruins of temples where worshippers once gathered.

facts: The earliest recorded games are usually dated to 776 BCE.
Ancient Greek pottery shows how some sports looked.

entries.title: What happens in an inning of baseball?
entries.answer: In baseball, one team tries to score while the other plays in the field. A batter can send the ball into play and then try to reach first base. Runners advance from base to base, and reaching home safely can score a run. The fielding team tries to get three outs. Then the teams swap jobs for the other half of the inning, so both have a chance to bat.
facts: Most Major League Baseball games are scheduled for nine innings. Some games end sooner or go longer under the rules.

entries.title: Why are there different swimming strokes?
entries.answer: In swimming, a stroke is a pattern of arm and leg movements that moves a swimmer through water. In front crawl, the arms take turns reaching and pulling. In backstroke events, the swimmer usually faces upward. In breaststroke, the arms move together and the legs make a kick that pulls in and sweeps out. Butterfly combines arms that swing through the air together with an up-and-down motion through the body and legs.
facts: In an individual freestyle race, the rules allow a choice of stroke, and most racers use front crawl.

entries.title: Why do hockey players use a puck?
entries.answer: Ice hockey players use curved sticks to move a flat rubber puck across the ice. Its flat face lets it slide, which helps players send it along the surface toward a teammate. Each side tries to put the puck in the other side’s net. Players push with the edges of their skates to speed up, slow down, and turn quickly. A goalkeeper guards each net.
facts: The whole puck must cross the goal line between the posts and under the crossbar for a goal, subject to the rules.

entries.title: Why does a badminton shuttle slow down so fast?
entries.answer: A badminton shuttle has a rounded base and a wide skirt made from feathers or a shaped material. A racket strikes the base. Air pushes against the wide skirt, helping turn the shuttle so the base goes in front and slowing it quickly after a hard hit. Players hit it back and forth over a net. They must return it before it touches the floor of their court.
facts: A badminton shuttle can be made with real feathers or a synthetic skirt.

entries.title: Why does a track cycling course tilt at the sides?
entries.answer: A velodrome is a closed oval track used for bicycle racing. The track is higher near the outside edges of the bends. The slope, called banking, makes part of the track’s upward push point inward. That helps racers follow the bend at high speed. The curve also means riders must choose when to speed up and where to pass. Different track cycling events ask riders to use speed, timing, and teamwork in different ways.
facts: Many top-level velodromes are 250 meters around, measured along the track’s marked measuring line.
